title: Level 3 Geography — Natural Processes and Landscapes 2025
subject: geography

questions.text:
Name a New Zealand geographic environment to use to answer both parts of the question.

Use the space provided to draw an annotated map(s) and/or diagram(s) of your environment to explain how interacting natural processes have shaped ONE natural feature.

questions.markingGuide: Achievement (N1-N2): Relevant natural feature identified with some supporting evidence. Partially analyses how processes interact to shape the feature. Merit (A3-A4): Includes some supporting case study evidence with some detail. Partially analyses the operation and interaction of processes to shape natural features. Excellence (M5-M6): Includes some detailed supporting evidence. Analyses the operation and interaction of processes to shape natural features of a NZ geographic environment.

questions.text:
Analyse how interacting natural processes operate in your environment to shape a second, different, natural feature from that identified in part (a).

Your response to part (b) should include:
- the name of your second natural feature — this must be different from the feature in part (a)
- how natural processes operate and interact to create and shape this second natural feature
- integrated comprehensive supporting case study evidence.

questions.markingGuide: Achievement (N1-N2): Describes natural processes and environment but provides little or no evidence. Merit (A3-A4): Includes some supporting case study evidence with some detail. Analyses the operation and interaction of processes. Excellence (M5-E8): Includes detailed supporting evidence. Analyses the operation and interaction of processes with insight, drawing conclusions. Integrates comprehensive evidence throughout. At E7-E8, analyses with insight the operation within a named NZ environment, drawing conclusions about natural features.
